statement: For an $m \times n$ matrix $\mathbf{A}$, the transpose $\mathbf{A}^{\text{T}}$ is the $n \times m$ matrix obtained by switching the row and column indices of $\mathbf{A}$, formally defined elementwise by $[\mathbf{A}^{\text{T}}]_{ij} = [\mathbf{A}]_{ji}$.

symbols.meaning: entry of matrix A at row j, column i
entry of transpose matrix A^T at row i, column j
number of rows in matrix A and columns in matrix A^T
number of columns in matrix A and rows in matrix A^T

properties.why: Transposing a scalar-multiplied matrix yields the scalar multiplied by the transposed matrix, making transposition a linear map
The order of factors in a matrix product reverses under transposition
The determinant of a square matrix is identical to the determinant of its transpose
The transpose of an invertible matrix is invertible and its inverse is the transpose of the original inverse
The dot product of column vectors can be evaluated as a matrix product using the transpose
Adjoint relationship for matrix-vector multiplication under the standard dot product
Each product is equal to its own transpose since (\mathbf{A}\mathbf{A}^{\text{T}})^{\text{T}} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{A}^{\text{T}}

properties.property: \mathbf{A}^{\text{T}}\mathbf{A} \text{ is positive-semidefinite if } \mathbf{A} \text{ has real entries}
properties.why: A real matrix multiplied by its transpose always forms a positive-semidefinite matrix

assumptions.assumption: \mathbf{A} is a well-defined matrix with entries arranged in m rows and n columns over a field or ring
assumptions.breaks_when: The dimensions or entries of the object are undefined or not organized in a 2D matrix structure

assumptions.assumption: \mathbf{A} and \mathbf{B} have compatible dimensions (e.g. m x k and k x p) for product transposition
assumptions.breaks_when: The number of columns of \mathbf{A} does not equal the number of rows of \mathbf{B}

assumptions.assumption: \mathbf{A} is a square matrix (m = n) when evaluating determinants, inverses, or eigenvalues

assumptions.breaks_when: \mathbf{A} is singular or has a determinant of zero

failure_modes.signature: Shape error or invalid multiplication when computing \mathbf{B}^{\text{T}}\mathbf{A}^{\text{T}}
failure_modes.cause: Attempting to compute (\mathbf{A}\mathbf{B})^{\text{T}} without reversing the order of the matrices, or when the inner dimensions of \mathbf{A} and \mathbf{B} do not match
Attempting to invert \mathbf{A}^{\text{T}} when \mathbf{A} has determinant zero or lacks full rank
Applying determinant equality \det(\mathbf{A}^{\text{T}}) = \det(\mathbf{A}) or eigenvalue properties to a non-square matrix
